ctx.x: Over the river when I was riding over the river.

Mm. Did you know a guy named Cooney? Cooney? Yeah. He was a Tom Anderson. There had been a woman. A singer. Cooney? Yeah, I know Cooney. Was it a man or a woman or what? It was a man. Cooney. Did he play an afternoon?

No, I never knew anything to play an afternoon. Cooney, I know. A lot of those guys, but I forget their names. It's like Louis White. When I was in France, I was sitting in the audience and an actress, she must have been a little bit of a woman. She asked, she said, is anybody here from the Orleans? I raised my hand up. I said, yeah, I'm from the Orleans. She said, well, come up here. I'm going to ask you something. And I went up there and I said, what do you want to ask her, miss? She said, I want to ask her,…

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: No, I never worked at Tom Anderson's, never did.

ctx.x: Did you ever work at Tom Anderson's too?

No, I never worked at Tom Anderson's, never did. Never did work at Tom Anderson's. But we used to see, when them times we used to go around and play, you know what I mean, for different people, you know. Yeah. And we used to go around and play just for fun, you know. I had the fellows that say, man let's go to my so and so's house today, you know. Pete would take his violin. I'd take my, I'd, sometime I'd take my banjo, sometime I'd tear the piano, I wouldn't take my banjo. I'd play the piano, you see what I mean?
Oh fine, now something you mentioned earlier, what year about would that be when you spoke about, you heard Jelly Roll more?
